title: POC Weekly Sync — Rollout / Go‑Live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout and go-live planning for NovaCommerce pilot. Discussed canary strategy (5-10%), A/B options, cutover window, monitoring & runbooks, rollback criteria, security sign-offs, and next steps including cost estimate and updated runbook draft.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM); Marta, Ethan, Priya, Jon (NovaCommerce)
---
[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — canary plan, cutover window, monitoring/runbook review, next steps. can we do a quick status?
[00:21] Marta: yeah thanks, we are at end of pilot week 3, results look promising. latency at 95th around 210-230ms on dev traffic, cost is still a bit higher than we'd like.
[00:35] Daniel: okay good, that aligns with our benchmark. just to call out the dev tests used the redwood-dedicated small GPU pool and the quantized variant. the KV cache hit rate was about 38% which we think we can push up with prefix caching.
[00:50] Ethan: hmm 38% — we spoke earlier about caching PRs, our traffic mix is bursty during checkout windows so cache hit varies. any ideas to stabilize?
[01:10] Daniel: yeah two things — cache warming at deploy, and we suggested a small warm-up canary that preloads common prefix sets. also the batching profile: for checkout flow we recommend a smaller max batch to keep p95 low — say 4-8 tokens per batch.
[01:35] Priya: on SRE side we care about spike behavior; whats the fallback if Dedicated capacity floods? elastic fallback to hosted?
[01:44] Aisha: correct — we can route overflow to hosted API as an emergency fallback, or to a cheaper quantized variant in the same pool. that is already in the routing policy we demoed.
[01:58] Jon: how would the canary look? percent and duration?
[02:05] Daniel: recommended start: 5% of user traffic for 24 hours, monitor p95, error rate, and business KPIs. if stable, bump to 10% for 48 hours, then 25% for another 24–48h before full cutover.
[02:20] Marta: any concerns with doing A/B instead? product team is leaning to A/B so we can compare model variants A (current) vs B (redwood variant).
[02:33] Aisha: A/B is fine but you lose the pure progressive fallback model; it's more of an experiment. for rollout safety canary gives cleaner rollback with routing policies. we can do an A/B within the 5% slice if you want both.
[02:50] Ethan: ok that sounds reasonable. what are the rollback criteria we should bake into runbook?
[02:58] Daniel: simple thresholds: p95 increases >20% vs baseline OR error rate >0.5% OR any customer-visible failures. also automated rollback if latency hit persists for >15 minutes after autoscaling.
[03:15] Priya: autoscaling — what's the expected cold-start on Dedicated? we saw warmup delays previously.
[03:24] Daniel: with the current pool config warmup is ~90s for a new worker; KV cache population is separate. recommend pre-scaling during the 10-minute cutover window.
[03:40] Lena: quick note — security/compliance, Marta, you flagged SOC2 docs last week, legal wants SSO & audit logs confirmed before prod. are we good there?
[03:52] Marta: legal needs the SOC2 attestation and the KMS/HSM flow for keys. also need clarity on data residency for EU customers.
[04:05] Aisha: we have SOC2 Type II cert, and repo of security docs — i'll share the security pack. KMS integration is supported; we can outline HSM flow in the runbook. i'll add data residency options for EU.
[04:18] Jon: cutover timing — we are thinking a Tue night to minimize traffic. any blackout windows?
[04:25] Ethan: we have a release freeze until midnight Tuesday, can do 00:30-02:00 PT maintenance window.
[04:32] Daniel: that window is fine. for the canary we suggest starting 00:30 with 5% ramp. if we need to rollback, the routing cutover rollback is near-instant.
[04:44] Marta: monitoring — what dashboards & alerts will be in place?
[04:49] Daniel: Redwood console will expose token-level latency, per-route p95, error rates, model quality metrics (we'll surface sampling of outputs). we'll add synthetic checks hitting checkout flow and a business KPI check (cart conversion delta).
[05:05] Priya: alerts — where do they page? Slack + PagerDuty?
[05:10] Aisha: yes, we'll integrate with your PagerDuty and post to ops slack channel. thresholds we'll propose and you can iterate.
[05:18] Ethan: runbooks — can we get a pre-filled runbook draft with exact rollback commands and owner steps?
[05:25] Daniel: yes, we'll provide a runbook template with step-by-step commands (route change CLI, scale-down, rollback to hosted endpoint, verification checks).
[05:35] Marta: cost — what's the expected incremental spend for the canary stages?
[05:40] Aisha: we'll run a quick cost calc. rough ballpark for 5% traffic on Dedicated small pool is ~ $1.8k/day, dependent on token volume. will send detailed cost sheet for 5/10/25% scenarios.
[05:56] Jon: any dependency on infra changes on our side?
[06:01] Daniel: only minimal: add routes for Redwood endpoints in your API gateway and ensure the auth tokens are available via K8s secret. we'll provide exact manifests.
[06:12] Marta: timeline — we want to go prod by next Thursday if everything looks good. is that feasible?
[06:20] Aisha: tight but doable. today's action items should get us there: security pack, cost sheet, updated runbook, and your traffic curve.
[06:30] Ethan: question on A/B quality checks — will Redwood surface semantic regressions? we need model quality fallback if outputs degrade.
[06:40] Daniel: yes, Redwood Optimize will run evals on a prompt set and can trigger alerts when quality drops beyond a threshold. we'll wire that into the canary checks. small caveat — semantic evals take a few hours to aggregate.
[06:58] Priya: ok good to know.
[07:05] Aisha: quick recap: 5% canary start 00:30 Tue, monitor p95 & errors, integrate PagerDuty + Slack, runbook draft + rollback criteria, security docs and KMS flow shared. next checkpoint Wednesday to confirm artifacts, final signoff Thursday morning.
[07:25] Marta: agreed. we'll get you the traffic profile and confirm blackout window.
[07:32] Jon: will also loop in infra for the gateway routes.
[07:38] Aisha: perfect. I'll send calendar invites for the cutover war room, and share the cost spreadsheet + runbook.
[07:45] Lena: i'll follow up on onboarding doc and scheduling the post-mort run after cutover.
[07:51] Ethan: any notes on vendor risk / competitors? legal asked if we considered Anthropic / OpenAI for redundancy.
[07:58] Aisha: we discussed multi-vendor routing earlier — Redwood can route to different providers, but for this pilot we recommend single vendor with hosted fallback to simplify metrics.
[08:10] Marta: ok thanks, wrapping up.
---
References shared: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (security docs), https://redwood.ai/costs/novacomm-canary-2026-09 (cost sheet - draft), runbook draft link: (sent in calendar invite).
